reasoning: This workflow reveals FairTix's intelligent support ticket triage system. When new support messages appear in a Google Sheet (likely from a form or email integration), Claude AI classifies them into 6 categories (FAQ, Account/Verification, Payment/Billing, Technical/Bug, Resale/Transfer, Feedback) with sentiment analysis. The switch node routes FAQ and Payment/Billing questions to automated responses using a Google Docs knowledge base, while other categories trigger manual escalation via Gmail. The sophisticated AI prompt shows deep domain knowledge of ticketing marketplace operations, with specific examples for edge cases like angry customers asking FAQ questions. With 88% success rate across 50 executions and 362 version iterations, this is clearly a production system under active refinement. The sheet-based architecture suggests integration with existing customer service tools or forms.
name: FairTix Support Ticket Classification and Auto-Response
businessNarrative: FairTix operates an intelligent customer support system that automatically triages incoming tickets and provides instant responses for common inquiries. The AI analyzes each message to determine both the support category and customer sentiment, routing FAQ and billing questions to automated responses while escalating complex issues to human agents. This reveals FairTix as a ticket marketplace dealing with queue fairness, resale policies, and payment processing — requiring sophisticated support categorization to handle the unique challenges of fair ticket distribution. The system reduces support team workload while ensuring urgent issues receive immediate human attention.
trigger: New row added to the Support Requests Google Sheet
dataFlow: Support messages enter via Google Sheet, get classified by Claude AI with category/sentiment/confidence scores, FAQ questions receive automated responses from Google Docs knowledge base, complex issues trigger Gmail notifications to support team, all responses and classifications are recorded back to the sheet.

impact.reasoning: Customer-facing support system that directly affects response times and customer satisfaction. Failure would result in unresponded tickets and invisible support issues, degrading customer experience. However, has manual fallback through direct support team contact.
impact.failureScenario: Support tickets would accumulate without classification or response, FAQ questions would require manual handling, support team wouldn't receive escalation notifications, leading to delayed responses and frustrated customers.
impact.revenueConnection: Indirect — poor support experience affects customer retention and marketplace reputation, but doesn't directly block transactions. Confidence: data-driven.

timeSavingsEstimate: 30-45 minutes per ticket for FAQ responses (benchmark-based: typical support agent handles 8-12 tickets/hour), plus classification time savings for escalated tickets.
